title: Lumbar stepwise resection
summary: Remove structures step by step as each study did and report rotation at the stated pure moment after every step.
simulate: Build the specimen of the view: lumbar FSU, disc-only unit, thoracic FSU, or C7-L1 spine with rib cage.
Fix the caudal vertebra; apply the pure moment (and preload, if stated) to the cranial end.
Remove structures cumulatively in the listed order; re-run the same load at every step.
Report rotation at peak moment: one direction, or full range (both directions summed) if stated.
For % of intact tasks divide by your own intact value and multiply by 100.

notes: Heuer and Wilke values are medians at one moment (Heuer 7.5 Nm, Wilke 2.5 Nm). Other moments (1-10 Nm), neutral zones, Wilke T2-T3 and T10-T11, and per-segment rib cage ROM (Liebsch 2017/2020) stay in bench/tests.
rom = one direction from the neutral posture; rom_range = both directions summed (thoracic spines with rib cage). Do not compare one with the other.

Left out: Rahm 2019 (T4-L2 screw-rod construct and cyclic loading, i.e. an instrumented specimen); Healy/Lubelski local-region ROM (n 5-7); Liebsch 2017 NZ; Heuer 2008 strain and bulge; Ghezelbash 2020 review load-sharing secondaries (moment shares, not ROM).
Healy 2014 and Lubelski 2014 come from one lab with similar torsos; listed as shared in case donors overlap (not stated).
agent_prompt: Use your finite element spine model. For each view build the specimen named in the task inputs (lumbar FSU, lumbar disc-only unit, thoracic FSU without ribs, or C7-L1 spine with rib cage). Fix the caudal end, apply the pure moment (plus preload if given) to the cranial end, and record rotation at peak moment. Then remove the structures in the listed order, cumulatively, and repeat the same load after every step. Output "rom" is rotation in one direction from neutral; "rom_range" is the sum of both directions (e.g. flexion plus extension), measured T1 relative to T12 unless the level says otherwise; "rom_pct" is your value divided by your intact value times 100. Return JSON with one entry per task id, as in answer_format, values in degrees or percent.
